rows.pairReadIllinois: The two Illinois sealing tracks were read side by side because 22 of their 26 rendered pages are byte-identical. I extracted all 26 pages of each family with pdftotext -layout and hashed page by page: pages 4 and 5 of BOTH the canonical and the boundary fixture differ; the other eleven pages of each fixture are identical text. The four differing pages carry exactly four differences, and I read every one of them on the page: (1) Request page 4, sealing table row 1, Charge cell -- 'Retail theft, Class A misdemeanor' vs 'Possession of a controlled substance, Class 4 felony'; (2) Request page 4, same row, Outcome cell -- 'MC' vs 'FC', which are the form's own printed Outcome Abbreviations for Sealing for Misdemeanor Conviction and Felony Conviction; (3) Request page 5, Section 17 ticked in il-seal-2yr-set and blank in il-seal-3yr-set; (4) Request page 5, Section 19.c ticked in il-seal-3yr-set and blank in il-seal-2yr-set. For each of the other 22 pages I read the page and can say why the two remedies do not differ there: Request pages 1-3 are the expungement branch, blank in both, and the form's own note above Section 1 tells a seal-only filer 'do not fill out this section', so the blank is the printed instruction and not an omission; Request page 6 is Sections 23-24 (trafficking, reckless driving), elected by neither, plus the verification, lawyer and official-use blocks; packet page 7 is the EXP-AD Case List, whose 78 AcroForm fields I enumerated with pdf-lib and which carries no charge, outcome, ground or election field at all -- only the caption and seventy unlabelled arrest-or-case cells, so the same case number produces the same page; packet pages 8-9 are the EXP-AD Order Granting, whose only case-specific fields are the expungement and sealing case-number grids and the recipient block, with no charge, outcome or ground field, so it too is legitimately identical; packet pages 10-13 are the FW-CIV-APPLICATION, which carries only the caption, name and contact details in both. Taking the Captain's list one at a time: ELIGIBILITY RECITALS are carried, on Request page 5. WAITING-PERIOD COMPUTATION is carried on page 5 and nowhere else, because none of the four official forms has a sentence-completion-date field or any arithmetic field; the period is asserted solely by the printed words of the elected limb ('2 years' in Section 17, '3 years' in Section 19.c). That is symmetric between the two and is the most the form allows. STATUTORY CITATION is on the face of NEITHER petition: the EXP-AD Request prints statutory cites only inside its own option text (Section 15, Section 18) and has no route-citation field, so no filing-face difference is possible or missing. The citation lives only in participant-instructions.md, and there it is asymmetric -- see the crossChecks entry. FILING DESTINATION, SERVICE and FEE are identical in both families' filing-instructions.md and participant-instructions.md, and correctly so: all three are 20 ILCS 2630/5.2 petition-level rules that do not vary with the waiting period. Destination is the circuit clerk of each county of arrest or charge under Section 5.2(d)(1); the CLERK serves under Section 5.2(d)(4) and the participant serves no one; the fee is a circuit clerk fee plus a $60 ISP order-processing fee, county-collected, with the Rule 298 waiver, and both packets ship the FW-CIV-APPLICATION. ANSWER: yes, the four pages carry the whole of what these two remedies differ by on the face of the filing. The pair is not a clone and I found no difference that belongs on one petition and is missing from it. The defect I did find is not between the two families but inside il-seal-2yr-set, and it is a ROUTE_OPTIONS failure scored on that family alone.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: The route declares five dispositions and the packet delivers one, presenting the other four as belonging to no route. data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, track il-seal-2yr, dispositions = ['supervision_successfully_completed', 'qualified_probation', 'conditional_discharge_completed_without_revocation', 'probation_completed_without_revocation', 'misdemeanor_conviction'], and its mechanism sentence reads 'a two-year sealing bucket effective June 1, 2026, covering successfully completed supervision, qualified probation, conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, and misdemeanor convictions'. Its own requiredBeforeFiling line asks the participant to check the answer to 'For each case, was the outcome supervision, qualified probation, conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, a misdemeanor conviction, or a felony conviction?' -- a multi-way question. The delivered Request page 5 prints all four two-year grounds: Section 16 (supervision, 2 years), Section 17 (misdemeanor conviction, 2 years), Section 18 (qualified probation / Cannabis Control Act Section 10 / Controlled Substances Act Section 410 / Meth Act Section 70 / Offender Initiative Program, 2 years) and Section 19.a (conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, 2 years). The packet ticks Section 17 only. production-field-map.json refuses Section 16, Section 18 and Section 19.a with the string 'A participant election or financial fact not determined by this packet route' and routeDetermined: false. That reason is untrue of this route: those three printed grounds ARE this route's other declared dispositions. participant-instructions.md never mentions Section 16, Section 18 or Section 19.a. It names only Section 17 and a negative election of Section 15. A participant on this track whose disposition is supervision, qualified probation, or unrevoked conditional discharge or probation -- four of the track's five dispositions -- is handed a petition that states the wrong ground and is told nothing about which box states theirs, on a document they verify under 735 ILCS 5/1-109. The sibling il-seal-3yr-set is the control and shows this is the factory's own standard: for its two three-year limbs it marks 19.b isAlternativeToElectedGround: true, gives 19.a and 19.b route-specific refusal reasons instead of the boilerplate, and devotes a guide section 'The Section 19 ground this packet ticked' to telling the participant to tick the other limb and untick this one if the certified record so shows. il-seal-2yr-set does none of that for any of its three alternative grounds. Corroborated by a second committed record: il-seal-3yr-set's own guide says of Section 19.a 'that is the two-year limb for a sentence of conditional discharge or probation that was NOT revoked, and it is a different route' -- naming 19.a as belonging to the two-year route that omits it.

REPEATING_ROWS.detail: The Request's Section 13 sealing grid is ten printed rows. Printed row 1 is complete in both fixtures -- all five cells written (Arrest or Case Number, Arresting Agency, Charge, Date of Arrest, Outcome) -- and rows 2 through 10 are wholly blank on the rendered page, with no partial row and no value on a row whose other cells are empty. The 'I have listed additional arrests or cases on the attached Additional Arrests or Cases for Sealing form' box is correctly unticked, since no additional form ships. The expungement grid on Request page 2 is blank in all ten rows, correct for a seal-only route. The Case List's seventy cells carry one case number in the first cell and nothing else. The Order's two case-number grids carry the same case number in the SEALING grid and nothing in the EXPUNGEMENT grid.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Both filing-instructions.md and participant-instructions.md state the fee structure without inventing a figure: a circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected; ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order; county totals commonly run roughly $60 to $235 with McLean County publishing $136; and 'Treat every figure as county-specific'. The waiver is named as Supreme Court Rule 298 with Section 5.2(d)(1) requiring no fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained. The FW-CIV-APPLICATION ships as pages 10-13 and the packet writes nothing on it beyond the caption, name and contact details; the guide says so explicitly and lists all 46 of its check boxes as the participant's, which I spot-checked against the rendered pages. The registry's own release blocker -- that no statewide county fee table exists -- is honoured rather than papered over, because no single figure is presented as the fee.

I token-diffed each of the 13 delivered pages against its pinned blank source page and every added token resolves to a declared write: caption and participant identity on packet pages 1, 7, 8; the sealing row on page 4; the elected ground tick on page 5; the signature-block identity and self-represented tick on page 6; the Order recipient block on page 9; the FW-CIV caption and name on page 10 and its signature block on page 13. PROTECTED_FIELDS.detail: The delivered fixtures carry no AcroForm at all: pdf-lib loads each and reports 0 fields and no /AcroForm in the catalog, so no field remains writable. Nothing court-owned was written. The map's declared-write set and its refusal set partition the 424 source fields exactly with no overlap, and every court/clerk/prosecutor-owned field -- including 'EXP-AD Request:7 - Case Number', refused as 'The form reserves this case number for the Circuit Clerk' -- is on the refusal side. CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: Measured by rendering, not by a counter. I rendered the boundary fixture's Request pages 4-6 at 110 dpi and looked at them. The boundary persona's long charge string ('Retail theft of property not exceeding three hundred dollars, Class A misdemeanor, with an extended statutory description that materially exceeds one line') and the long arresting-agency string auto-shrink and wrap to three and two lines respectively, entirely inside the printed row-1 cell borders, and do not touch row 2. The long name, e-mail and address on the signature block wrap onto the printed rule and do not overprint the 'Street, Apt. # / City / State / Zip Code' labels. No value is ellipsized anywhere in either fixture. No glyph crosses a cell border on any page I rendered.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: All eight selfHelpStopConditions on the registry track are present verbatim in participant-instructions.md under 'Stop and get help', checked one by one by exact whitespace-normalised string containment, and the guide adds that two of them -- a federal or out-of-state record and a denied petition -- this packet cannot help with at all.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: filing-instructions.md and participant-instructions.md both name the circuit clerk of each county where an arrest occurred or a charge was brought, a separate packet per county, Cook County to the district matching the case, and e-filing where the county requires it. That matches the registry destination object ('Circuit clerk of the county of arrest or charge') and the venue paragraph citing Section 5.2(d)(1). No residence-county language anywhere.

SERVICE.detail: The guide names the method, the recipients and the objection period: the circuit court clerk serves under Section 5.2(d)(4) and the participant serves no one; notice goes to the State's Attorney, the Illinois State Police, the arresting agency and, for municipal ordinance violations, the chief legal officer; the objection period is 60 days from service under Section 5.2(d)(5)(B), and absent objection the court shall enter an order under Section 5.2(d)(6)(B). This is a Section 5.2 petition-level rule and is correctly identical to the sibling Illinois sealing track.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: All ten requiredBeforeFiling lines on the registry track are present verbatim in participant-instructions.md, checked by exact whitespace-normalised containment. The Request's verification block is deliberately blank on the delivered page and the guide says so in terms, names the wet-signature expectation and cites 735 ILCS 5/1-109. The prior FAIL on this obligation is repaired: the sentence VF02 quoted at line 22 -- 'Make the per-case expunge or seal election in the Case List's per-case election column' -- is gone, and the guide now states that the shipped Case List has no election column, enumerates its 78 fields, and says the election was made on the Request instead. I verified that claim independently by enumerating the Case List's fields with pdf-lib: 78, none of them an election field.

ARTIFACTS.detail: The prior ARTIFACTS FAIL is repaired and I re-measured rather than adopting the claim. Reloading each delivered fixture with pdf-lib and resolving every page's /Annots entry against the document returns 21 annotation references and ZERO unresolvable ones on both fixtures (VF02 measured 146 dangling per fixture on the previous bytes); all 21 are /Link subtype, the ilcourts.info hyperlinks carried by the source form. PAGE_ORDER.detail: Read across document boundaries, not only within each document. The delivered order is primary_filing (ATJ 2901.9 pages 1 of 6 through 6 of 6), attachment (ATJ 2902.1 page 1 of 1), proposed_order (ATJ 2905.6 pages 1 of 2 and 2 of 2), fee_waiver (FW-CIV pages 1-4), which matches the declared component order 1-2-3-4 in both the registry packetSet and product-wiring.json. Every document's own printed 'Page n of m' footer runs in sequence with no gap and no repeat, and each boundary falls exactly where the previous document's last printed page number says it should.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: The registry track il-seal-3yr declares dispositions ['felony_conviction', 'conviction_not_captured_by_two_year_category'] and the form prints exactly two three-year limbs, Section 19.b (revoked conditional discharge or probation, 3 years) and Section 19.c (completed Illinois prison or jail sentence, 3 years). The packet elects 19.c and presents 19.b as the route's own alternative in both records: production-field-map.json refuses 19.b with 'The other printed three-year ground. This packet elects the Section 19 limb the certified record supports and leaves this one blank; tick this one instead, and untick the other, if the certified record shows a revoked sentence of conditional discharge or probation' and marks it isAlternativeToElectedGround: true, and participant-instructions.md carries a dedicated section saying the same in the form's own words. It also correctly excludes 19.a with a route-specific reason naming it as the two-year limb and a different route. Both of the route's printed options are therefore represented.

REPEATING_ROWS.detail: The Request's Section 13 sealing grid is ten printed rows. Printed row 1 is complete in both fixtures -- all five cells written (Arrest or Case Number, Arresting Agency, Charge, Date of Arrest, Outcome) -- and rows 2 through 10 are wholly blank on the rendered page, with no partial row and no value on a row whose other cells are empty. The 'I have listed additional arrests or cases on the attached Additional Arrests or Cases for Sealing form' box is correctly unticked, since no additional form ships. The expungement grid on Request page 2 is blank in all ten rows, correct for a seal-only route. The Case List's seventy cells carry one case number in the first cell and nothing else. The Order's two case-number grids carry the same case number in the SEALING grid and nothing in the EXPUNGEMENT grid.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Both filing-instructions.md and participant-instructions.md state the fee structure without inventing a figure: a circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected; ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order; county totals commonly run roughly $60 to $235 with McLean County publishing $136; and 'Treat every figure as county-specific'. The waiver is named as Supreme Court Rule 298 with Section 5.2(d)(1) requiring no fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained. The FW-CIV-APPLICATION ships as pages 10-13 and the packet writes nothing on it beyond the caption, name and contact details; the guide says so explicitly and lists all 46 of its check boxes as the participant's, which I spot-checked against the rendered pages. The registry's own release blocker -- that no statewide county fee table exists -- is honoured rather than papered over, because no single figure is presented as the fee.
